newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: CRH to buy BTR's Tilcon, sets placing.
newsitem.headline: CRH to buy BTR's Tilcon, sets placing.

text.p: Irish building materials group CRH Plc is buying Tilcon Inc from BTR Plc for a gross consideration of $329 million and announced a placing of 17.94 million shares to raise a net 101 million punts.
CRH said in a statement that it had acquired the entire issued share capital of Tilcom for a consideration of $220 million or 135.8 million Irish pounds.

CRH said it will also assume responsibility for Tilcon's net debt at August 31, 1995. This is estimated at $109 million or 67.3 million and reflects the impact of high-seasonal working capital. No goodwill arises in connection with the acquisition.
The consideration will be satisfied by drawing from CRH's existing dollar resources and long-term facilities which were augmented by a $440 million U.S. private placement concluded in May, CRH said.
CRH said that at average working capital levels, net debt would be around $25 million lower than that being assumed at August 31.

Disposal of a Connecticut quarry and asphalt plant and the planned sale of two non-core businesses and surplus assets were expected to realise $50 million, making the net effective cost of the acquisition $254 million or 156.8 million punts.

Commenting on the acquisition, CRH said Tilcon represented a unique and very exciting opportunity to strengthen the position of Oldcastle, the holding company for CRH's North American operations, in the northeastern states.
"This region, with its severe climatic conditions, generates a high demand for road repair and maintenance," Oldcastle chief executive Liam O'Mahony said.
"Tilcon is an excellent fit with our existing operations giving the enlarged materials group unrivalled coverage in this key market area," he said.

O'Mahony said CRH hopes to be able to realise very significant operating synergies by integrating Tilcon into its materials group, thereby generating trading profit margins of the order of 10 to 12 percent.

Tilcon, headquartered near Hartford, Connecticut, is one of the largest construction materials groups in the northeastern U.S. Following the acquisition, CRH's enlarged materials group will have annualised sales of more than $800 million, CRH said.
In 1995, Tilcon reported an operating profit of $33 million on sales of $369 million while pre-tax profit came to $27.8 million, CRH said.

CRH also announced a placing of 17.94 million new ordinary shares of 25 Irish pence each to raise 101 million Irish pounds net of expenses to assist the funding of the group's future development programme.
Although Tilcon is larger than CRH's usual add-on acquisitions, the group said its development strategy remained unchanged.

"The equity placing combined with the group's strong cash flow should ensure adequate funding for the continuation of CRH's devolved development strategy in North America, Europe, and new developing regions where local development teams continue to generate good value adding opportunities," it said.
